summary: Administration of Business Central online: how tenants and environments are run, managed, licensed, monitored with telemetry, supported and migrated to. It answers questions from internal admins and delegated partners on admin center tasks, permissions, onboarding, deployment, telemetry, APIs, support and cloud migration.
overview:
This section is for administrators of Business Central online tenants, whether they work inside the customer organization or as delegated partners. The landing page introduces the main tasks: user management, permissions assignment, licensing, environment updates, telemetry and partner relationships.

The subtopics split the work by task. "Understand Business Central online" explains the service itself (tenants, environment types, update cycles, version numbers, limits, availability, trials, reseller and delegated admin access, and support). "Admin center" covers day-to-day environment management and includes an Admin Center API subtopic. "Entitlements and permissions" covers access control and licensing. "Prepare Business Central" and "Onboard your customers" cover getting an environment ready and shaping first use. "Monitor and analyze telemetry" and "Manage technical support" cover monitoring and escalation. "Migrate to Business Central online" covers moving on-premises data to the cloud. The Automation API (55 pages) and Cloud Migration API (26 pages) subtopics cover those two APIs.

Start with "Understand Business Central online" if the service is new to you. Go to "Admin center" for environment tasks. Use "Entitlements and permissions" for access and license questions. Use the telemetry and migration subtopics for those specific projects.
key_points: The landing page covers user management, permissions assignment, licensing, environment updates, telemetry and delegated administration for partners.

Admin center pages cover creating, copying, renaming, deleting, restoring, exporting and transferring environments. They also cover apps, updates, access, capacity, telemetry, sessions, notifications and consumption-based billing.
Entitlements and permissions explains how entitlements, permissions and permission sets differ. It also covers license plan structure and the SUPER, D365 BASIC and SYSTEM APP permission sets.

Prepare Business Central covers setup overview, configuration packages, Excel and Outlook add-ins, deploying and upgrading extensions, app key vaults, and managing upcoming and newly mandatory features.
Onboarding pages cover trials, the SignupContext parameter, the welcome banner, checklist, teaching tips, tours, recommended apps and onboarding telemetry.
Telemetry goes to Azure Application Insights. Pages cover enabling it, event IDs, KQL and Power BI analysis, alerts and cost control.
Technical support pages cover troubleshooting tools, escalating to Microsoft, and reporting performance problems and production outages.
Migration covers paths from Business Central, Dynamics NAV, GP, SL and custom SQL sources, with FAQ and troubleshooting. Separate subtopics cover the Automation API and the Cloud Migration API.

issues: Key point on Prepare Business Central says "mandatory upcoming features". The source says "managing upcoming and newly mandatory features", so the wording changes the meaning.
The Automation API and Cloud Migration API subtopics are described as API reference material. The inputs give only their titles and page counts and no summaries, so their content type is a guess.

Minor: the overview leaves out that "Understand Business Central online" also covers version numbers and reseller and delegated admin access, and that Admin center has an Admin Center API subtopic. These are omissions, not errors.
